title: India's 4,000-Year-Old Port
description: Lothal in Gujarat: a Harappan port town with what may be one of the world's earliest docks.

scenes.narration: Over four thousand years ago, boats were docking here, in Gujarat.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient brick dock basin with wooden boats, Indus valley port town, morning

scenes.narration: This is Lothal, a port town of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
scenes.image_prompt: aerial view of an ancient Harappan brick town with grid streets beside a river

scenes.narration: Its huge brick basin is thought by many archaeologists to be one of the world's earliest dockyards.
scenes.image_prompt: large rectangular brick basin filled with water and boats, workers unloading

scenes.narration: Beads made from carnelian travel all the way to Mesopotamia.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient trader holding red carnelian bead necklaces, cargo jars, boat

scenes.narration: Streets are laid out in a grid, with drains running along them.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Harappan street with covered brick drains and houses, people walking

scenes.narration: Workshops make beads, shell jewellery and copper tools.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient bead makers drilling carnelian beads in a workshop, shell bangles

scenes.narration: Seals carved with animals and a script we still can't read mark the goods.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of square Indus seal with unicorn-like animal and script signs, clay

scenes.narration: The Indus script is still not deciphered. Do you think we'll ever read it?
scenes.image_prompt: Lothal archaeological site today, brick remains under blue sky
